assumedContext: No primary filing retrievable; findings rest on the Q3 FY2026 earnings release and FY2025 results.
Fiscal year ends 30 September. FY2026 revenue of ~EUR 45bn is derived from FY2025's EUR 39.1bn and guided comparable growth of 14-16%.

findings.claim: Q3 FY2026 was a record on every line: orders EUR 17.9bn, revenue EUR 11.4bn (+18.5% comparable), profit before special items EUR 1,623m at a 14.2% margin, and net income EUR 1,188m, up more than 70% year on year.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Siemens Energy Q3 FY2026 earnings release

findings.claim: FY2026 guidance: comparable revenue growth of 14-16% and a profit margin before special items of 10-12%, with management trending to the upper end. On FY2025 revenue of EUR 39.1bn that implies roughly EUR 45bn of revenue and roughly EUR 5.2-5.4bn of profit before special items.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE
findings.source: Siemens Energy FY2026 outlook, confirmed at Q3

findings.claim: The scale of the turnaround is the story the thesis undersells. FY2025 profit before special items was EUR 2,355m at a 6.0% margin and net income EUR 1,685m. FY2026 guides to roughly EUR 4bn of net income — a doubling in one year, on a margin that has also doubled.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Siemens Energy FY2025 results and FY2026 guidance

findings.claim: The finding that drives this dossier, and it repeats GE Vernova's exactly. FY2026 free cash flow pre-tax is guided at around EUR 8bn against net income of around EUR 4bn and profit before special items of roughly EUR 5.3bn. Management attributes the increase explicitly to customer advance payments and reservation fees associated with the strong order intake.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE
findings.source: Siemens Energy FY2026 outlook and Q3 FY2026 commentary

findings.claim: The mechanism is arithmetic, not accounting doubt. Book-to-bill of 1.57x means customers are prepaying against orders faster than the company converts them to revenue. When book-to-bill approaches 1.0x the advance pool stops growing and free cash flow converges toward profit plus depreciation — roughly EUR 5.5bn pre-tax rather than EUR 8bn.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the disclosed book-to-bill and cash flow drivers

findings.claim: The difference from GE Vernova is one of degree, and it favours Siemens Energy. GE Vernova guides free cash flow at roughly twice adjusted EBITDA; Siemens Energy guides it at roughly 1.5x profit before special items. The distortion is present in both and materially smaller here.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived; cross-reference to the GE Vernova dossier in this batch

findings.claim: Demand classification: the EUR 162bn backlog is [Existing Contracted]; the FY2026 guidance is [Management Guidance] and largely covered by that backlog; continued 1.5x book-to-bill through 2028 is [Approved / Committed Pipeline] on the demonstrated intake rate; and the assumption that current margin levels persist beyond the capacity build is [Speculative Demand] earning zero base-case weight.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The credit market has already ratified the operational turnaround: Moody's reaffirmed Baa1 and moved the outlook to positive in June 2026, and S&P upgraded to BBB+ stable in July 2026.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Rating agency actions, June and July 2026

risks.text: Roughly EUR 2.5bn of the guided EUR 8bn free cash flow is customer advances on a still-growing order book, and it stops accruing when book-to-bill reaches 1.0x.
The margin doubled in one year. Extrapolating that rate is the mistake the price would have to be making for this to be expensive.
Guidance is on profit before special items, and the special items run rate is not established here.

catalysts.text: First quarter in which book-to-bill falls below 1.2x
Completion of the second EUR 1bn buyback tranche

conclusions: The operating turnaround is real and large: margin before special items has roughly doubled from 6.0% to a guided 10-12% at the upper end, and net income roughly doubles to about EUR 4bn.
Q3 was a record quarter on orders, revenue, margin and net income, and the credit agencies have ratified it with an S&P upgrade to BBB+ and a positive Moody's outlook.

The finding that drives the valuation is the same one found at GE Vernova: free cash flow pre-tax is guided at around EUR 8bn against roughly EUR 5.3bn of profit before special items, and management attributes the difference to customer advance payments on record order intake.
At 1.57x book-to-bill the advance pool is still filling. At 1.0x it stops, and underlying free cash flow converges toward roughly EUR 5.5bn pre-tax — a gap of about EUR 2.5bn a year.
The distortion is materially smaller here than at GE Vernova, which guides free cash flow at roughly twice adjusted EBITDA. Siemens Energy guides it at roughly 1.5x profit before special items.
thesisImpact: Phase 3 establishes that the DCF must be run on underlying free cash flow of roughly EUR 5.5bn pre-tax, not the guided EUR 8bn. Using the headline figure would overstate fair value by roughly 40%. That single adjustment is the difference between this dossier's answer and the sell-side consensus.
